title.en: Transfer Learning: Standing on Giants' Shoulders

description.en: Use pre-trained models like ResNet and fine-tune them for custom tasks with minimal data and training time.
description.ta: ResNet போன்ற முன்-பயிற்சி பெற்ற மாதிரிகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி, குறைந்தபட்ச தரவு மற்றும் பயிற்சி நேரத்துடன் தனிப்பயன் பணிகளுக்கு fine-tune செய்யுங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Shortcut

Vaathiyaar shows a child who already knows to ride a bicycle. "Teaching this child to ride a motorcycle is much easier than teaching from scratch. Transfer learning is the same — take a model trained on millions of images and adapt it to your specific task."

### Transfer Learning Strategy

1. Load a pre-trained model (trained on ImageNet: 1.2M images, 1000 classes)
2. Freeze early layers (they detect universal features: edges, textures)
3. Replace the final classification layer
4. Fine-tune on your dataset

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torchvision.models as models

# Load pre-trained ResNet-18
model = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT)

# Freeze all layers
for param in model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False

# Replace the final fully connected layer
num_features = model.fc.in_features  # 512
model.fc = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(num_features, 128),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Dropout(0.3),
    nn.Linear(128, 5)  # 5 custom classes
)

# Only train the new layers
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.fc.parameters(), lr=0.001)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

print(f'Total parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}')
print(f'Trainable: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad):,}')

# Training loop (same as before)
model.train()
for epoch in range(10):
    for images, labels in train_loader:
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        outputs = model(images)
        loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
```

### Fine-tuning (Unfreeze some layers)
```python
# After initial training, unfreeze last few layers for fine-tuning
for param in model.layer4.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = True

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam([
    {'params': model.layer4.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-4},  # low lr for pre-trained
    {'params': model.fc.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-3}       # higher lr for new layers
])
```

> **Key Insight:** With transfer learning, you can achieve 95%+ accuracy on custom datasets with just a few hundred images!
story_variants.ta:
## வாத்தியாரின் குறுக்கு வழி

வாத்தியார் ஏற்கனவே சைக்கிள் ஓட்ட தெரிந்த குழந்தையைக் காட்டுகிறார். "இந்த குழந்தைக்கு மோட்டார்சைக்கிள் ஓட்ட கற்றுக்கொடுப்பது புதிதாக கற்றுக்கொடுப்பதை விட மிகவும் எளிது. டிரான்ஸ்ஃபர் லேர்னிங் அதே போன்றது."

explanation.en: Load ResNet-18 pre-trained on ImageNet (1.2M images, 1000 classes). Already knows edges, textures, objects

steps.line: for param in model.parameters(): param.requires_grad = False

explanation.en: Freeze all layers — don't update pre-trained weights during training
Get the input size of the original final layer (512 for ResNet-18)
Replace the 1000-class head with our 5-class head. Only these new layers will train
Only optimize the new fc layers — saves time and memory
Only 0.6% of parameters are trainable! 99.4% leverage pre-trained knowledge

steps.line: for param in model.layer4.parameters(): param.requires_grad = True

explanation.en: Fine-tuning: unfreeze the last conv block to adapt features to our domain
Use lower learning rate for pre-trained layers to avoid destroying learned features
Higher learning rate for new layers that need to learn from scratch

steps.line: # 10 epochs is often enough with transfer learning!

explanation.en: Transfer learning converges much faster than training from scratch — often 5-15 epochs

executionSteps.explanation: Freeze all layers — keep learned features
Only 2,565 params to train — fast fine-tuning!

instruction.en: PyTorch cannot run in this sandbox, so this is the numpy version of what PyTorch does under the hood. Do transfer learning by feature extraction: keep a pre-trained backbone frozen and train only a new classification head (fine-tuning would also update the backbone). The starter code gives you the frozen `W_backbone` and a 5-category dataset. 1) `extract_features(X, W_backbone)` returns relu(X @ W_backbone). 2) `train_head(features, y, num_classes, lr=0.1, epochs=300)` trains a softmax classifier with gradient descent: start W = zeros((n_features, num_classes)), b = zeros(num_classes); each epoch compute p = softmax(features @ W + b), grad = (p - one_hot(y)) / n, then W -= lr * features.T @ grad and b -= lr * grad.sum(axis=0); return (W, b). 3) `predict(features, W, b)` returns the argmax class per row. The backbone must stay unchanged.
instruction.ta: இந்த sandbox-ல் PyTorch இயங்காது, எனவே இது PyTorch உள்ளே செய்வதன் numpy பதிப்பு. Feature extraction மூலம் transfer learning செய்யுங்கள்: pre-trained backbone-ஐ frozen ஆக வைத்து, புதிய classification head-ஐ மட்டும் பயிற்றுவியுங்கள் (fine-tuning backbone-ஐயும் update செய்யும்). Starter code-ல் frozen `W_backbone`-உம் 5 வகை dataset-உம் உள்ளன. 1) `extract_features(X, W_backbone)` relu(X @ W_backbone) திருப்புகிறது. 2) `train_head(features, y, num_classes, lr=0.1, epochs=300)` gradient descent மூலம் softmax classifier-ஐப் பயிற்றுவிக்கிறது: W = zeros((n_features, num_classes)), b = zeros(num_classes) என்று தொடங்கி, ஒவ்வொரு epoch-லும் p = softmax(features @ W + b), grad = (p - one_hot(y)) / n கணக்கிட்டு, W -= lr * features.T @ grad, b -= lr * grad.sum(axis=0) செய்யுங்கள்; (W, b) திருப்புங்கள். 3) `predict(features, W, b)` ஒவ்வொரு வரிசைக்கும் argmax class-ஐத் திருப்புகிறது. Backbone மாறாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.

practice_challenges.starter_code:
import numpy as np


def relu(x):
    return np.maximum(0, x)


def softmax(z):
    e = np.exp(z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True))
    return e / e.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)


def make_dataset(n, seed):
    """Synthetic 'images' (20 features) from 5 categories."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    centers = np.random.default_rng(42).standard_normal((5, 20)) * 2
    y = rng.integers(0, 5, n)
    return centers[y] + rng.standard_normal((n, 20)) * 0.5, y


# Stand-in for a pre-trained ResNet backbone: fixed weights learned "elsewhere".
W_backbone = np.random.default_rng(7).standard_normal((20, 32)) / np.sqrt(20)


def extract_features(X, W_backbone):
    # frozen backbone: relu(X @ W_backbone)
    pass


def train_head(features, y, num_classes, lr=0.1, epochs=300):
    W = np.zeros((features.shape[1], num_classes))
    b = np.zeros(num_classes)
    # gradient descent on the softmax cross-entropy - only W and b change
    # Your code here
    pass


def predict(features, W, b):
    # most likely class for every row
    pass


X_train, y_train = make_dataset(300, seed=1)
X_test, y_test = make_dataset(100, seed=2)
backbone_before = W_backbone.copy()
F_train = extract_features(X_train, W_backbone)
F_test = extract_features(X_test, W_backbone)
head = train_head(F_train, y_train, num_classes=5)
if head is None:
    print("train_head() returned None")
else:
    W_head, b_head = head
    acc = np.mean(predict(F_test, W_head, b_head) == y_test)
    print("trainable parameters (head only):", W_head.size + b_head.size)
    print("frozen backbone parameters:", W_backbone.size)
    print(f"test accuracy with a frozen backbone: {acc:.2f}")
    print("backbone unchanged:", np.array_equal(W_backbone, backbone_before))

practice_challenges.test_code:
import numpy as np
_Xa, _ya = make_dataset(200, seed=11)
_Xb, _yb = make_dataset(100, seed=12)
_Wb = W_backbone.copy()
_Fa = extract_features(_Xa, _Wb)
assert _Fa is not None and np.shape(_Fa) == (200, 32), "features must have shape (n_samples, 32)"
assert np.allclose(_Fa, np.maximum(0, _Xa @ _Wb)), "extract_features must return relu(X @ W_backbone)"
_h = train_head(_Fa, _ya, num_classes=5)
assert isinstance(_h, tuple) and len(_h) == 2, "train_head must return (W, b)"
_W, _bb = _h
assert np.shape(_W) == (32, 5) and np.shape(_bb) == (5,), "the head must map 32 features to 5 classes"
assert np.array_equal(_Wb, W_backbone), "the backbone is frozen - training the head must not change it"
_pred = predict(extract_features(_Xb, _Wb), _W, _bb)
assert _pred is not None and np.shape(_pred) == (100,), "predict must return one class per row"
assert np.mean(_pred == _yb) > 0.9, "the trained head should reach over 90% accuracy on new data"
_one = train_head(_Fa, _ya, num_classes=5, epochs=1, lr=0.1)
_ref_grad = (np.full((200, 5), 0.2) - np.eye(5)[_ya]) / 200
assert np.allclose(_one[0], -0.1 * _Fa.T @ _ref_grad), "one epoch must apply W -= lr * features.T @ ((p - one_hot) / n)"
print("All transfer-learning tests passed!")

q.en: Why do we freeze early layers in transfer learning?
q.ta: Transfer learning-ல் ஏன் ஆரம்ப அடுக்குகளை freeze செய்கிறோம்?

en: Early layers detect universal features (edges, textures) useful for all tasks
To prevent the model from learning
ta: ஆரம்ப அடுக்குகள் அனைத்து பணிகளுக்கும் பயனுள்ள உலகளாவிய அம்சங்களைக் கண்டறிகின்றன

q.en: What is the recommended learning rate strategy for fine-tuning?
q.ta: Fine-tuning-க்கு பரிந்துரைக்கப்படும் learning rate உத்தி என்ன?

en: Same high lr for all layers
Lower lr for pre-trained layers, higher lr for new layers
Highest lr for the first layer
ta: Pre-trained அடுக்குகளுக்கு குறைந்த lr, புதிய அடுக்குகளுக்கு உயர்ந்த lr

q.en: How many images do you typically need for effective transfer learning?
q.ta: பயனுள்ள transfer learning-க்கு பொதுவாக எத்தனை படங்கள் தேவை?

en: Hundreds to a few thousand per class
ta: ஒரு வகுப்புக்கு நூற்றுக்கணக்கான முதல் சில ஆயிரங்கள்

under_the_hood.summary: Transfer learning reuses a network already trained on ImageNet as a feature extractor: its early layers keep their learned weights, the 1,000-class output layer is replaced with a small head for your classes, and only the new parts (or a few top layers) are trained.

steps.title: Pre-trained features are general
steps.body: A ResNet-18 trained on about 1.2 million ImageNet images has early filters for edges and colours, middle ones for textures and parts, and late ones for object-level features. Those are useful for flowers, X-rays or products too, so you start from them instead of from random weights.

steps.title: Swap the head
steps.body: models.resnet18(weights=...) ends with fc = Linear(512, 1000). The lesson replaces it with Linear(512, 128), ReLU, Dropout(0.3), Linear(128, 5). The body still turns any image into 512 numbers; the new head learns to map those to your 5 classes.

props.caption: New head on top of the 512 pre-trained features (scaled down)

steps.title: Freeze, then train only the head
steps.body: Setting requires_grad = False on the backbone's parameters stops gradients there, and passing only model.fc.parameters() to Adam means only the head changes. That is 66,309 trainable numbers instead of about 11.2 million in the backbone, so a few hundred images per class and a few epochs can be enough.

props.caption: Parameters for ResNet-18 with the lesson's head

steps.title: Feed it images the way it learned
steps.body: The backbone expects inputs prepared like ImageNet: resized and cropped to 224 x 224 and normalised with mean [0.485, 0.456, 0.406] and std [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]. Using other statistics shifts every activation and quietly costs accuracy. The weights object's transforms() returns the matching preprocessing.

steps.title: Optionally fine-tune deeper
steps.body: Once the head has learned, you can unfreeze the last block (layer4) and continue with a smaller learning rate, often 10 times lower, so the pre-trained features adapt gently instead of being overwritten. The more your images differ from ImageNet and the more data you have, the more layers it pays to unfreeze.

nodes.label: unfreeze layer4, train with lower lr

under_the_hood.takeaway: Transfer learning starts from features someone else paid to learn. Replace the head, match the original preprocessing, train the new layers first, and unfreeze more only when your data justifies it.
